builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Efficient Secure Federated Learning via Information-Theoretically Secure Key Distribution: A Medical Imaging Case Study
summary: The method replaces uncompressed federated model updates under additive masking with a combination of frozen backbones, knowledge distillation, and quantization to shrink the communication payload that must be encrypted with rate-limited, information-theoretically secure keys. It costs training flexibility, since backbones are frozen and a distilled student model is used, and adds framework complexity across compression, secure aggregation, and key buffer management. It can fail if key generation rates drop below even the reduced consumption rate, if quantization or distillation degrades accuracy on a different medical task, or if the deployment lacks access to a physics-based key distribution testbed entirely.
rationale: The method addresses a niche constraint (finite key generation rates in information-theoretically secure key exchange for cross-institution federated learning) that only arises with specialized quantum or physics-based key distribution hardware and a multi-party FL deployment, neither of which fits a single-GPU or API-based practitioner.
technique: Payload compression for ITS-secure federated learning

claims.statement: The method replaces uncompressed federated model updates under additive masking with a combination of frozen backbones, knowledge distillation, and quantization to shrink the communication payload that must be encrypted with rate-limited, information-theoretically secure keys. It costs training flexibility, since backbones are frozen and a distilled student model is used, and adds framework complexity across compression, secure aggregation, and key buffer management. It can fail if key generation rates drop below even the reduced consumption rate, if quantization or distillation degrades accuracy on a different medical task, or if the deployment lacks access to a physics-based key distribution testbed entirely.
Reduces cryptographic key material consumption by approximately 35x while maintaining chest X-ray classification accuracy, preventing key buffer depletion on a physics-based key distribution testbed.
